title: Gauss AGM Iteration and Elliptic Integrals
description: The arithmetic-geometric mean (AGM) iteration of Gauss: given a ≥ b > 0, iterate aₙ₊₁ = (aₙ+bₙ)/2, bₙ₊₁ = √(aₙbₙ). Both sequences converge to a common limit M(a,b). The deep result: M(1,√(1-k²)) = π/(2K(k)) connecting AGM to complete elliptic integrals.

meta.author: Carl Friedrich Gauss (1799)
meta.assumptions: 3 axioms: completeEllipticK (definition of K(k)), completeEllipticK_pos (K(k) > 0), gauss_agm_elliptic (AGM = π/(2K(k))). The elliptic integral connection is axiomatized because Mathlib lacks elliptic integral theory. AGM convergence has 2 sorries for the final limit argument.

overview.historicalContext: Gauss discovered the AGM iteration around 1799 and proved its connection to elliptic integrals, calling it one of his most remarkable discoveries. The AGM provides the fastest known algorithm for computing π (Brent-Salamin, 1976) and elliptic integrals. The iteration doubles the number of correct digits at each step due to quadratic convergence.
overview.problemStatement: Define the AGM iteration for positive reals a ≥ b, prove convergence to a common limit M(a,b), and state the connection to complete elliptic integrals of the first kind.
overview.text: The arithmetic-geometric mean iteration converges quadratically. The sandwich property bₙ ≤ bₙ₊₁ ≤ aₙ₊₁ ≤ aₙ ensures both sequences are monotone and bounded, hence convergent. The gap aₙ - bₙ contracts by at least half each step.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. Define AGM sequences (mutual recursion).
2. Prove positivity by joint induction.
3. Prove AM ≥ GM for two reals (key: (x-y)² ≥ 0).
4. Derive sandwich: bₙ ≤ bₙ₊₁ ≤ aₙ₊₁ ≤ aₙ.
5. Prove gap contraction and convergence.
6. Axiomatize the elliptic integral connection.
keyInsights: Both AGM sequences are monotone and bounded, hence convergent by the monotone convergence theorem
The gap aₙ - bₙ contracts by at least half each step, forcing convergence to a common limit
AM ≥ GM at each step provides the sandwich: bₙ ≤ bₙ₊₁ ≤ aₙ₊₁ ≤ aₙ
The connection M(1,k') = π/(2K(k)) transforms elliptic integral computation into simple iteration

sections.title: AGM Iteration Definition
sections.summary: Mutually recursive definition of the AGM arithmetic and geometric sequences.

sections.title: Positivity
sections.summary: Both sequences stay positive when started with positive values.

sections.title: AM ≥ GM Sandwich
sections.summary: AM ≥ GM at each step gives the sandwich property bₙ ≤ aₙ.

sections.title: Monotonicity
sections.summary: a-sequence decreasing, b-sequence increasing, full sandwich theorem.

sections.title: Convergence
sections.summary: Gap contracts, both sequences converge to common limit M(a,b).

sections.title: Elliptic Integral Connection
sections.summary: Axiomatized: M(1, √(1-k²)) = π/(2K(k)) — Gauss's deep identity.

conclusion.text: The AGM iteration is formalized with its key convergence properties. The sandwich property (bₙ ≤ bₙ₊₁ ≤ aₙ₊₁ ≤ aₙ) and gap contraction are proved from first principles. The connection to elliptic integrals is axiomatized pending Mathlib support for elliptic integral theory.
opens: Prove AGM convergence without sorry (using Mathlib monotone convergence)
Formalize the elliptic integral K(k) and prove the AGM connection
conclusion.implications: The AGM provides the fastest known method for computing π and elliptic integrals.
